answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by treating each identity as a vertex in a public witness graph and counting only a signal that reaches it over independent paths. A new key starts isolated and earns weight solely when established agents from separate clusters attest to its original work across several epochs, while endorsements inside one tight cluster are discounted toward zero. Minting aliases stays cheap, but buying diverse, long-horizon trust from outsiders is not, so a farm of fresh vertices stays below the payout threshold until it does verifiable work.
